title: Security Deposit Account Move-Out Inspection and Itemization Standard
content:
Move-out charges on a Security Deposit Account are itemized only while the account is in move-out review. Review starts on the lease's move-out date. The account status is read from the account's own record.

## 1. What may be itemized

Only three kinds of charge may be itemized: damage beyond normal wear and tear, cleaning, and the per-unit charges below.

Normal wear and tear is never charged. It includes paint faded or lightly scuffed by ordinary living, a few small nail holes, carpet worn along traffic paths, sun-faded blinds, and loosened fixtures.

## 2. Cleaning

Cleaning is itemized once, for the whole unit. It is itemized only when the inspection finds the apartment home not left as clean as it was at move-in. It is never itemized when the program waives the cleaning charge.

The schedule of cleaning charges by floor plan is:

| Floor plan | Cleaning charge (USD) |
|---|---|
| Studio Residence | 125.00 |
| One-Bedroom Residence | 150.00 |
| One-Bedroom Den Residence | 165.00 |
| Two-Bedroom Residence | 195.00 |
| Three-Bedroom Residence | 235.00 |
| Penthouse Residence | 295.00 |

*Retired clause.* The words pricing the cleaning line "at the cleaning charge for the lease's floor plan" are **no longer in force**. They are superseded by the current basis for the cleaning charge.

*Retired clause.* The clause "stains beyond normal cleaning add the program's carpet spot-cleaning charge per room" is **no longer in force**. It is superseded by the current basis for the spot-cleaning rate.

## 3. Replacements

*Retired clause.* The clause charging a carpet, paint, flooring, blinds or appliance replacement at its replacement cost times the remaining useful life, divided by that useful life, is **no longer in force**. That clause took the remaining life as the item's useful life under the program less its recorded age, never below 0, rounded half up to the cent on the straight-line monthly method. It is superseded by the current basis.

In force: an item at or past its useful life is never charged.

## 4. Damage repair and per-unit charges

*Retired clause.* The clause pricing a damage repair line as its labor hours, rounded up to the program's labor increment, times the program's labor rate, plus the parts cost recorded as its replacement cost, is **no longer in force**. It is superseded by the current basis.

*Retired clause.* The clause "unreturned fobs are the quantity times the program's unreturned fob charge" is **no longer in force**. It is superseded by the current basis.

In force: trash or abandoned-property removals are the quantity times the program's trash removal charge.

## 5. Conditions on every line

- **Photos.** A line above the program's photo evidence threshold may be itemized only when dated move-out inspection photos of the item are on file. The photos must match this account, this charge category and this room.
- **Pre-move-out inspection.** A pre-move-out inspection is offered a set number of days before the intended move-out date. An item listed at that inspection which the resident corrected before moving out may not be charged.
- **One line per category per room.** Only one line per charge category per room is itemized. A second line of the same category in the same room of the same account is not itemized.

### Illustrations (hypothetical)

- **Wear and tear.** Carpet worn only along the hallway traffic path is not charged.
- **Photo threshold.** On a program whose photo evidence threshold is 100.00 USD, a 140.00 USD line with no dated inspection photos on file may not be itemized. A 90.00 USD line needs no photos.
- **Removals.** Two trash removals on a program whose removal charge is 150.00 USD come to 300.00 USD.
- **Duplicate line.** A second cleaning line for the kitchen of the same account is not itemized when one already exists.
